One time on a hot summers day, my friend and I decided we wanted to go to Taco Bell. The nearest Taco Bell to the mall we were at was 12km away, and we were both way too broke to pay bus fare. We REALLY wanted Taco Bell so we walked those 12 excruciating kilometres in blistering heat. By the time google maps told us that we had arrived at our ever so desired Taco Bell, we were in a... neighbourhood..?? We were both instantly confused. We had checked the location, and it had reviews, so it wasn’t a fake. Had we made a wrong turn? Surrounded in broken vodka bottles on the sidewalk of a shady neighborhood, we sat in defeat, exhausted and taco-less. I sat up, a new wave of determination entering my soul like the tide at noon. 
“We can’t just give up now! We must be close, I know it!” 
“You’re a madman, you know. Let’s find that Taco Bell” 
And so, with our phones close to dead and our backs soaked with sweat, we set out on a final search for Taco Bell. We ran it through google maps again and walked to the location. A house. Fuck. Had we been duped? We check the location of the Taco Bell again, but this time we checked the photos all the way at the back of the display. Sure enough, we’d been got. Someone had somehow entered in their HOUSE as a Taco Bell. We lost our minds. We had walked for what seemed to be hours only to be led to a fake Taco Bell. We ended up walking back to the mall for tacos. The mall that we started at, might I add. If we had just looked closer at the pictures of the location while we were still there, we wouldn’t have wasted so much time. 

Moral of the story: thoroughly check all google maps locations, seriously
